spin_from_markers — DRIVE balltrack op

• Data kinds: points × points → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.spin_from_markers(dirs0, dirs1, dt: 'float') -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import balltrack; balltrack.spin_from_markers(dirs0, dirs1, dt: 'float') -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("spin_from_markers"))

Usage

Angular velocity vector ω [rad/s] from pairs of marker directions (before (M, 3), after (M, 3), unit vectors).

If M ≥ 2, fit the rotation R by Kabsch (SVD) and compute ω = θ/dt·axis from the rotation angle θ and the axis (feeding directions rotated by a known ω returns it to 1e-9 = gate). If M = 1, return the minimal rotation d₀ → d₁ (axis = d₀ × d₁) ("full" = False): the component about the marker direction is undeterminable in principle, and if the rotation angle between frames is large it also fails as an approximation of the orthogonal component of ω (the marker traces a small circle about the ω axis, which differs from the great circle of the minimal rotation).

Honestly: to get ω from a single marker, make dt small (rotation angle ≪ 1 rad); even then the component about the axis needs another marker. Return value {"omega", "angle", "axis", "R", "full", "rms"}.
